# Intake brief — Full-suite runs dirty the main checkout ship-config.csv

> **Source request (verbatim):** "Full-suite test runs (observed with
> changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leave
> src/data/ship-config.csv modified in the MAIN checkout
> (thrustAcceleration/maxSpeed/frictionDeceleration/controlScheme changes),
> even though the suite runs from a worktree. A test exercising
> GymPlayer.saveShipConfig writes through the dev-server CSV plugin whose root
> resolves to the main checkout (likely via the symlinked node_modules / vite
> project root). This trips the implement dirty-tree gate on later sessions,
> requiring a git checkout restore; it can also silently clobber an operator's
> tuned ship config. … add a guard so suites never write the repo's tracked
> CSV."

## Headline

Full-suite test runs leak writes to the tracked `src/data/ship-config.csv` in the **main checkout** even when the suite runs from a worktree, breaking the implement dirty-tree gate and risking silent clobbering of an operator-tuned ship config. Fix the dev-server CSV plugin's root resolution and add a guard so suites never write a tracked repository CSV.

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite (observed during changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leaves `src/data/ship-config.csv` modified in the MAIN checkout — `thrustAcceleration`/`maxSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration`/`controlScheme` diverge from the committed values — despite the suite having run from a worktree. The only writer of the tracked CSVs is the dev-server CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`): its write handler resolves `resolve(root, 'src/data/ship-config.csv')` where `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274), and the config store's dev-mode save (`saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves`, gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is `true` under vitest) issues a **relative** `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (`src/core/configStore.ts` lines 397–405, 569–586). In vitest's happy-dom integration project (default `window.location` = `http://localhost:3000`, verified in the installed vitest source), happy-dom's fetch resolves relative URLs against that origin — so a real (un-mocked) save PUTs to `http://localhost:3000/api/csv/...`; whatever server answers there can write through a root that points at the main checkout. Worktrees symlink `node_modules` to the main checkout (confirmed on four live worktrees), which lets Vite's project-root/package-root inference escape to the main checkout. The worktree's own `csv-seed.test.ts` reads its CSVs via `__dirname`, so a leaked write to the *other* checkout is not caught by the seed tests in the active checkout. Consequences: the implement dirty-tree gate fails on later sessions (manual `git checkout` restore required), and an operator-tuned ship config can be silently clobbered; it likely also explains intermittent `csv-seed` / `<suite exited 1>` smoke failures (AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL, AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP, AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2).

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents running the suite** — "As a developer I want suite runs to never modify tracked config files in any checkout, so the implement dirty-tree gate stays green and I don't have to restore files manually."
- **Designers/operators tuning ship config** — "As a designer I want my tuned `ship-config.csv` to survive test runs, so my balance work isn't silently overwritten."
- **Test suite maintainers** — "As a test author I want tests to exercise save behaviour against isolated fixtures, so the suite is deterministic and hermetic."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).
2. **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.
3. **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.
4. **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.
5. **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

## Constraints

- Dev-only behaviour is preserved: while `npm run dev` runs from the active checkout, gym Save/Save As must still persist through the plugin to the committed CSVs (read-write dev workflow, AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA). Production builds stay read-only (`apply: 'serve'`).
- Atomic-write semantics (temp file + rename) and the post-save registry re-read (`reReadRegistry`) must be preserved on the success path.
- Test isolation is a requirement, not an option: current unit/integration tests already pin temp fixtures via explicit `root`; the gap is the default path and the dev-mode relative fetch. Do not weaken existing fixture patterns.
- Worktree isolation rules apply: implementation happens in a worktree; the main checkout is never edited directly.
- UK English for prose/comments; Markdown for work-item and code-doc prose.

## Existing state

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `configCsvPlugin(options)`: `const root = options.root ?? process.cwd();` (line 274); `handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath), …)` for ship/enemy/difficulty CSVs. Registered in `vite.config.ts` with no options (`configCsvPlugin()`, so default root = `process.cwd()` of the dev server / test process).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isDev()` = `import.meta.env.DEV === true` (line 97); `fetchCsv`/`putCsv` use relative `/api/csv/...` URLs (lines 397–405, 569–586); `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` (lines ~612–660) gate only on `isDev()`.
- Vitest config (`vitest.config.ts`) — `unit` (node) and `integration` (happy-dom, default origin `http://localhost:3000`) projects; `isolate: true`; the full suite is `unit` + `integration`.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` (lines 80, 121–133) and `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — real plugin behind an ephemeral HTTP server against a **temp** root with an explicit fetch bridge; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` / `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — `vi.mock('../../core/configStore')` replacing `saveShipConfig` with an in-process registry seed; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reads CSVs via `__dirname`, i.e. relative to the **active** checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it.
- Worktree layout — `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with `node_modules` symlinked to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed on four live worktrees: wl-AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40-*, wl-AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V-*, wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q-*, wl-AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C-*).

## Desired change

1. Make the plugin's write root explicit and safe: derive it from the Vite server's resolved project root (with an explicit override option), and refuse any write whose target resolves outside the active root. This removes the unpredictable `process.cwd()` default.
2. Add a store-level test-mode guard so the vitest harness can never write tracked files (registry-only no-op or temp-fixture routing), closing the relative-fetch escape route at the source.
3. Harden regression coverage: a suite-run cleanliness assertion (pre/post `git status` on both checkouts) plus unit tests for the new root guard and the test-mode guard.
4. Document the safe patterns (explicit roots, fetch bridges, module mocks) alongside the plugin and store modules.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — replace the `process.cwd()` default root with an explicit/Vite-resolved root that is verified against the active checkout; add the escape-refusal guard; update `ConfigCsvPluginOptions` docs.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for default-root behaviour (must not write outside active root) and the escape-refusal guard.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add test-mode detection to `isDev()`/save guards; document relative-fetch + bridge pattern.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` / `configStore.integration.test.ts` — tests for test-mode save no-op/temp routing; fixture pattern comments.
- `vite.config.ts` — pass an explicit root derived from `server.config.root` if the plugin cannot self-derive it.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — optionally extend the seed check to also assert a clean worktree/main-checkout diff (the suite-run cleanliness guard may live here or in a new small test).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (only if behaviour changes; otherwise untouched) — `_onSave` consumes `saveShipConfig`'s `ok/reason`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole": where the leak was first observed (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL** — "[test-failure] csv-seed.test.ts / configStore.integration.test.ts — ship-config.csv diverges from DEFAULT_CONFIG": the smoke symptom of a leaked write (`thrustAcceleration 390` vs `300`).
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** — "enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests)": sibling symptom on the enemy CSV.
- **AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP**, **AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2** — "[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test": possibly same intermittent root cause.
- **AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA** (config-store epic), **AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP** (CSV plugin), **AH-0MUE2MIK9001TK88** (integration tests) — origin of the dev write-back design being hardened here.
- **AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V** — "Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart": dev-server persistence semantics for ship config.
- **AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4** — "Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block": another save-path quirk.
- **AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM** (open) — "Dev-mode write-back: gym Save to repo persists bot tuning": the same "dev writes to tracked repo data" family; keep separate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-broad guard breaks the legit dev save flow** — mitigation: scope the refusal to (a) targets outside the active root and (b) test-mode; the dev-mode save path from the active checkout must keep working (AC2 keeps explicit-root fixtures valid).
- **Stray server on the happy-dom origin (localhost:3000) still receives writes if only the plugin changes** — the store-level test-mode guard (AC3) is the belt-and-braces fix; do not rely on the plugin alone.
- **Root-cause mechanism partially inferred** — the exact process that answers the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run was not reproduced deterministically in this intake; the implementer must reproduce and confirm before finalising the guard wording (record the reproduction in the work item). Non-blocking for the fix: ACs are observable-outcome based.
- **Scope creep** — protecting against an operator's accidental save overwriting a tuned config in the *browser/UI* (e.g. a confirmation prompt) is a separate UX concern; record it as a separate item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption** — `npm --silent test` remains the audit-accepted full suite; suite runs from implement worktrees use symlinked node_modules; vitest happy-dom default origin is `http://localhost:3000` and happy-dom resolves relative fetches against it (verified in installed `vitest`/`happy-dom` sources at intake time).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (title + description of AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) already contained the observed symptom, the primary hypothesis (root resolution via symlinked node_modules / vite project root), and the suggested fix directions. Research performed during intake:

- **Q (self): "Which code path is the only writer of the tracked CSVs?"** — Answer (Map): `configCsvPlugin.handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath))` in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`; `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274). Source: code inspection of `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (plugin registered without options).
- **Q (self): "How does a suite-run write escape the temp-fixture pattern?"** — Answer (Map): all plugin instantiations in tests pass explicit temp roots (`configCsvPlugin.test.ts` line 100/447, `configStore.integration.test.ts` line 80) and GymPlayer tests mock the store — so the leak is not from these; the store's dev-mode save issues a relative `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (configStore.ts lines 397–405, 569–586) gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV` (true under vitest). In the happy-dom integration project, happy-dom's `Fetch` resolves the relative URL against `window.location.href` (verified in `node_modules/happy-dom/lib/fetch/Fetch.js`), whose vitest default is `http://localhost:3000` (verified in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` line 343). A real server on that origin with a root at the main checkout receives the PUT.
- **Q (self): "Why does the worktree's root resolve to the main checkout?"** — Answer (Map): worktree `node_modules` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed via `ls -la` on four live worktrees), so Vite's package-root/workspace-root detection and any module-relative path resolution can escape to the main checkout. Likely, not yet reproduced end-to-end (recorded in Risks).
- **Q (self): "Why doesn't the active checkout's csv-seed test catch the leak?"** — Answer (Map): `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` reads CSVs via `resolve(__dirname, …)`, i.e. the active checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it. Source: code inspection.
- **Q (self): "Are there existing related items?"** — Answer (Map): yes — AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL (ship-config smoke failure), AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT (enemy-config analogue), AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP / AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2 (generic suite-exit-1), AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V, AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4, AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM. Source: `wl search` during intake step 2.
- **Open question for the implementer (not a producer blocker):** reproduce the exact answering server/process on the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run and record it; the ACs are outcome-verifiable regardless.

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops — plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2 upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed** from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons` and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).
- AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y — Show current upgrades on the hull-full screen (open; same "player must see what they own" UI concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** celebration VFX/audio for the spin and rebalancing the
  1/5/10/84 split are follow-ups — record as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption (cap-aware draws):** when a drawn kind has hit its level cap,
  re-draw a non-capped owned kind; if every owned kind is capped the spin
  grants a fallback (minerals). Confirm during planning.
- **Assumption (mandatory spin):** the wheel always grants something and has
  no skip/decline path (a refusable "reward" recreates the perceived-nothing
  outcome).
- **Risk (unlock removal):** deleting the unlock feature removes a shipped
  progression mechanic; GDD §4.4.4 and the locked-pool docs must be rewritten
  in the same change so no doc promises unlocks. `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump
  invalidates existing checkpoints (accepted: pre-release).
- **Risk (resolver/UI drift):** the wedge list and the weighted outcome must
  be derived from the same owned-kind snapshot; the scene must never compute
  probabilities itself.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of unlock rewards.** "The wheel shows icons of power-ups the
  player has; should it fully replace the current upgrade-or-unlock choice
  (removing the run-scoped weapon-unlock feature, its locked-pool options and
  the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field)?" — **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply): Option A — fully replace.** The mini-boss reward becomes purely the
  upgrade wheel; unlock machinery is removed and `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` is
  bumped. Supersedes the options B (locked weapons as wheel outcomes) and C
  (separate secondary unlock offer). Source: producer answer, this intake
  session; recorded as AC5.
- **Q2 — Wheel population and empty-owned fallback.** "Should the wheel show
  **all** owned permanent kinds across the shared 6-slot pool (power-up kinds
  **and** weapon drops), and what happens at a mini-boss defeat when the
  player owns nothing permanent (possible at the level-1 mini-boss)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — all owned permanent
  kinds; when none are owned, fall back to the existing three-option
  hold-full-style choice so a mini-boss always pays. Options B (power-ups
  only) and C (seed the wheel with base entries) rejected. Source: producer
  answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1 + AC4.
- **Q3 — Wheel visual and weights.** "Should the wheel be 100 literal wedges,
  or a compact wheel (one wedge per owned icon + bonus wedge) whose spin
  outcome is weighted by the 100-slot distribution (1/5/10/84)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — compact wheel plus
  weighted outcome: legible UI, exact distribution preserved, multi-upgrades
  pick distinct kinds where possible. Options B (literal 100-wedge wheel) and
  C (proportional fixed wheel, accepting granularity loss) rejected. Source:
  producer answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1/AC3.

## Related-work check (duplicate detection)

Duplicate check performed (`wl search "mini-boss reward"`, `wl search
"wheel"`): no overlapping open item found — the closest items
(AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH, AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F, AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ,
AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) are completed/in-progress parents whose scope this item
extends or replaces; no duplicate.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH** – Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (completed)
- **AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD** – Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the player (completed)
- **AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y** – On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, 0mvlijt3m005hphf (+367 more)

## Plan (plan skill — 2026-10-28)

### Feature breakdown (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Child work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|-----------------|------|------------|
| 1 | Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver (AH-0MVSF5WXQ0035NW0) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver (AH-0MVSF5YKS000J0VZ) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Remove the weapon-unlock reward feature and bump checkpoint version (AH-0MVSF60BA002R47M) | task | — |
| 4 | Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin behaviour (AH-0MVSF61YO0002KE5) | task | — |
| 5 | Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene (AH-0MVSF63LN008YHMT) | feature | 2, 4 |
| 6 | Test the PlayScene wheel reward flow and empty-owned fallback (AH-0MVSF65AG007HITF) | task | — |
| 7 | Rework PlayScene mini-boss reward to the wheel (AH-0MVSF670W008RXEO) | feature | 2, 3, 5, 6 |
| 8 | Prove gym↔game parity for the mini-boss wheel reward (AH-0MVSF68QS006C8V0) | task | 5, 7 |
| 9 | Document the wheel reward and unlock removal (AH-0MVSF6AU40094YOM) | docs | 3, 7 |
| 10 | Verify the full test suite passes with the wheel reward (AH-0MVSFFXBY00668UJ) | task | 7, 8 |

### Key planning decisions (documented assumptions)

- **D1 — The launcher resolves the outcome; the overlay only animates it.**
  `PlayScene` draws one run-seeded outcome per defeat through `miniBossWheel`
  and hands the wheel scene the wedge list plus the resolved outcome. The
  overlay never computes probabilities, so the wedge list and the weighted
  outcome can never drift (AC1/AC3/AC6; mirrors how the choice pool is a
  single catalogue-derived source).
- **D2 — No level-cap filter on wheel draws (parity with the hold-full
  choice).** `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) offers
  level-ups with no cap check, and the run-scoped level stores are unbounded —
  only the *derived stat* saturates asymptotically
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`). A spin
  therefore always raises the run-scoped level and always pays out (producer
  confirmed Option A on 2026-10-28 — no level-cap filter).
- **D3 — Bonus = +1 level on every owned permanent kind** (AC3), applied
  through the shared reward seam.
- **D4 — Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer, 2026-10-28): the landing
  wedge of a multi-upgrade outcome shows **all** the gained kinds' icons
  present inside that one wedge**, so the complete result is legible at the
  pointer; extra gained kinds are not lit up on separate wedges. The overlay
  still applies the whole outcome exactly once. (Supersedes the earlier
  "extra wedges light up + results line" default.)
- **D5 — Empty-owned fallback reuses the shared hold-full three-option
  choice** (`chooseOptions` through `MineralChoiceScene`), applied
  permanently, so a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- **D6 — The wheel spin replaces the beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown** as the
  tension beat; the reduced-volume ghost-fire metronome and the beat-clock
  rebase on resume are retained for parity with the hold-full overlay.
- **D7 — Unlock removal lands before the PlayScene rework** (same files;
  smaller, reversible change first).
- **D8 — Test-first pairs share one branch.** Each red test item and its
  paired implementation item land together (tests committed first in branch
  history, red-for-the-right-reason recorded in a comment); the test item
  closes once the implementation makes it green. This is the only ordering
  that satisfies both test-first planning and the mandatory
  build → test → commit gate.
- **D9 — The eight former locked weapons remain ordinary catalogue weapons**
  reachable through the normal choice/drop paths (`CHOICE_POOL` /
  `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`); only the run-scoped unlock gate and its offer are
  removed — no dead content.

### Vertical slice phasing

Each child is a deliverable end-to-end slice with its own tests and docs:
(1–2) pure core with unit tests and module JSDoc; (3) feature removal with
fixture updates; (4–5) overlay scene with scene tests and registration;
(6–7) game integration with PlayScene plus demo-mode tests; (8) gym parity
surface with parity assertions; (9) documentation. The pure-module pair is a
library-first slice by nature (math + tests + JSDoc) — flagged here so
reviewers know the narrow layer is intentional.

### Acceptance-criteria coverage

AC1 → children 4, 5, 6, 7 · AC2 → 4, 5, 7 · AC3 → 1, 2, 4, 5 · AC4 → 6, 7 ·
AC5 → 3, 9 · AC6 → 1, 2, 5, 7, 8 · AC7 → 9 · AC8 → 1, 4, 6, 8.

## Resolved plan questions (producer answers, 2026-10-28)

- **Q1 — All-capped fallback (risk "cap-aware draws").** ANSWER (producer):
  **Option A** — no level-cap filter; the wheel matches the hold-full choice
  exactly and levels always increment, so a spin always pays out. Matches the
  adopted default D2; no change required.
- **Q2 — Multi-upgrade reveal.** ANSWER (producer): **the wedge with the
  multi-results has all icons present** — the landing wedge of a
  multi-upgrade outcome renders every gained kind's icon inside that one
  wedge; extra gained kinds are not lit up on separate wedges. Recorded as D4;
  affects the overlay scene (items "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin
  behaviour" and "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene").
- **Q3 — Spin duration/tension curve.** ANSWER (producer): **as recommended**
  — ≈2.2 s total, fast start (~3 rotations/s) easing out with at most one
  overshoot revolution, the duration exported as a constant for tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session, 2026-10-28)

- Q1–Q3 (intake) are answered by the producer and recorded in the intake
  Appendix above — not re-asked.
- Q4 = "Should the wheel re-draw away from level-saturated kinds, and what is
  the fallback when every owned kind is saturated?" — **Answer (producer,
  interactive reply, 2026-10-28): Option A** — no level-cap filter; parity
  with the hold-full choice, a spin always pays out. Final: A; adopted default
  D2 unchanged. Evidence: `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`
  (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) has no cap filter; `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  saturate derived stats (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`).
- Q5 = "How are simultaneous 2–3 upgrades revealed on a one-pointer wheel?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-28): the wedge with the
  multi-results has all icons present** — the landing wedge renders every
  gained kind's icon inside it; no separate wedge highlights. Final: adopted
  as D4. This does not change which wedges exist (still one per owned kind +
  bonus); it changes the *reveal* inside the landing wedge.
- Q6 = "What spin duration/tension curve should the wheel use?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-28): as recommended** — ≈2.2 s
  total, fast start (~3 rotations/s) easing out with at most one overshoot
  revolution, duration exported as a constant for tests. Final: as
  recommended.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 — plan skill: re-ran the duplicate check ("mini-boss reward",
  "wheel") — no overlapping open item; decomposed the parent into 9 children
  (4 test-first red items, 3 implementation features, 1 parity task, 1 docs),
  wired 11 dependency edges, and appended this Plan block, the OPEN QUESTIONS
  and the plan-session Appendix.
- 2026-10-28 — AC coverage review: parent ACs reflowed to single-line items;
  coverage 100% (proceed). The review auto-created two gap items: the docs gap
  was a duplicate of the docs child and was closed; the full-suite gap was
  rewritten into the final verification child (row 10, wired last).
- 2026-10-28 — producer answered the three plan questions (Q1 = A:
  no level-cap filter; Q2 = the multi-results wedge shows all gained icons;
  Q3 = as recommended). OPEN QUESTIONS section replaced with the resolved
  answers; D4 updated to the producer's multi-icon landing-wedge reveal;
  related child ACs updated.

# Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA) — intake brief

## Headline

Give the Railgun its missing audio identity: a baked ToneForge launch cue and a
baked per-weapon hit cue, both routed through the existing shared weapon-fire
and weapon-impact seams so live play, the hold-full metronome and every gym
sound identical — with no behaviour or balance change.

## Scope

SFX only: a **launch cue** (`playWeaponFireSound` → new `playRailgunFireSound`)
and a **hit cue** (`impactFx.cue` → new `playRailgunImpactSound`, which also
brings the minimal sky-blue impact-flash colour the seam needs to route the
cue). The Railgun's **muzzle-flash VFX is deliberately out of scope** — the
tracer's in-flight identity is already strong, and the launch cue carries the
audibility — tracked as Railgun launch muzzle-flash VFX
(AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K).

## Problem statement

The Railgun (`railgun`, one of the five net-new unlock-pool weapons from
AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW) is a slow, sky-blue, five-target-piercing tracer that fires
once every four beats (3000 ms at 80 BPM) and crosses ~490 px of arena. It looks
like a rail shot but it is **silent**: `playWeaponFireSound()`
(`src/audio/effects.ts`) has no `railgun` case, so the dispatch falls through to
the no-op `default:`, and the weapon definition declares no `impactFx`, so
`CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early and every connect lands with
no hit cue and only the generic warm-white fallback flash. The single most
dramatic shot in the game therefore has less feedback than the Cannon.

## Users

- **Player, mid-run** — "When I hold the Railgun I want to hear the shot leave
  the hull and hear it land, so the 3-second wait for the next shot feels like a
  charging rail, not a dropped input."
- **Player, holding a full weapon set** — "When the Railgun is one of several
  active weapons I want to pick it out of the mix by ear, the same way I can pick
  out the Wave Laser's beam crack."
- **Player at the hold-full overlay** — "The reduced-volume ghost fire should
  include the Railgun, so the beat keeps sounding while I choose."
- **Developer / gym author** — "The Railgun must sound the same in `PlayScene`,
  `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling` because they share one code path, not
  because three switches were kept in sync by hand."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible launch, one shared path.** `playWeaponFireSound('railgun')` routes
  to a new exported `playRailgunFireSound()` backed by a newly baked ToneForge
  cue (`aihell-railgun-fire`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome (via
  `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) and gym fire all sound identical through the
  existing single dispatcher; the `default:` no-op no longer applies to the
  Railgun.
- **Audible, per-weapon impact.** The `railgun` catalogue entry declares an
  `impactFx` spec (sky-blue `BULLET_COLORS.railgun` family, a radius/duration
  sized to the tracer, `cue: 'playRailgunImpactSound'`) resolved through
  `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` with a new baked hit cue
  (`aihell-railgun-impact`), so each pierced enemy connect is audible and
  sky-blue-tinted instead of the generic warm-white fallback flash.
- **Cue character is distinct and identifiable.** The launch cue reads as a
  heavy electromagnetic discharge (a deep, punchy snap/charge with a metallic
  transient), audibly different from the Wave Laser's 1200→600 Hz beam crack and
  the Cannon's 800→400 Hz thump; the hit cue is a short metallic crack with a
  brief ring, short enough (≲0.15 s) that a five-target pierce chain reads as
  one crisp salvo rather than a machine-gun stutter.
- **ToneForge pipeline complete and documented.** `aihell-railgun-fire` and
  `aihell-railgun-impact` recipe YAMLs exist under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`,
  are listed in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` as `baked` with recorded
  reserved seeds, render through `scripts/build-audio.sh --render`
  (`build-audio:verify` passes), and are recorded in the two mapping tables of
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (cue→consumer and recipe→seed).
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in shared code (`src/audio/`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`); no scene-level switch is added or forked. The
  Railgun's cues are exercised identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and
  `GymWeaponLeveling`, and `CombatScene.equivalence` plus the catalogue roster
  guards pass unchanged.
- **GDD roster updated.** The GDD §4.4 Railgun row (§7.3 weapon-cue list where
  applicable) and the README weapon roster mention the Railgun's launch and hit
  cues, so the weapon is no longer documented as visual-only.
- **No balance or behaviour change.** Fire rate (3000 ms / once per four beats),
  offsets (`[0]`), pass-through budget (`maxHitPoints` 5), bullet speed, size,
  colour, shape, lifetime and reach are unchanged; the change is audio plus the
  minimum impact-flash metadata needed to carry the hit cue.
- **Audio is a safe no-op headless.** With no `AudioContext` (tests, headless
  capture) both new cues degrade to silent no-ops; nothing throws.
- **Tests.** New/updated tests cover the fire dispatch case, the impact-cue
  registry entry, the `impactFx` metadata (and that `resolveWeaponDefinition`
  carries it through levelling unchanged), the impact-flash colour resolved by
  the shared seam, and the cue manifest contract.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, including the audio
  contract suite (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) and
  `build-audio:verify`.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments, README, and the GDD §4.4/§7.3 and audio-doc entries above.

## Constraints

- **Baked, not synthesised.** ToneForge assets are rendered at build time
  (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the only runtime-synthesised exception), so new
  cues require recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh --render` run, and the
  seeds must be recorded and pinned in the docs/tests.
- **Feel only.** Any balance or behaviour change discovered while adding the
  cues must be filed as a separate work item, not absorbed here.
- **Pipeline shapes are fixed.** Fire cues must route through
  `playWeaponFireSound`; hit cues must route through `impactFx.cue` →
  `playWeaponImpactCue`. No per-weapon playback path, no per-scene switch.
- **Gain staging.** New cues stay within the existing weapon-cue gain
  conventions and below the audio-balance-guard peak ceiling (0.5).
- **Voice limiter.** The shared per-cue limiter caps 4 concurrent voices per
  150 ms; a 5-target pierce chain may drop the deepest hits — acceptable by
  design, but the cue must be short so the chain does not smear.

## Existing state (audit evidence)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound()` handles cannon, spread, dual,
  rapid, nova, mortar, arc, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options; `railgun`
  (and `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`) fall to the
  explicit no-op `default:`. `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES` lists nine impact cues;
  no railgun entry.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — the `railgun` entry (`~line 1319`) has shape
  (`tracer`, length 8, thickness 2.2, trail 4.5, size 1.15), sky-blue
  `BULLET_COLORS.railgun = 0x66aaff`, `maxHitPoints: 5`, cadence
  `WEAPON_RAILGUN_SUBDIVISION = 0.25`, lifetime `1.4` (~490 px) — and **no**
  `muzzleFlash`, **no** `impactFx`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `resolveWeaponImpactFx()` is a no-op without
  `impactFx`; the non-lethal single-hit path then falls back to the generic
  `spawnBulletImpact` warm-white flash (`0xfff2a0`, r7).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/` — 50+ recipes, no `aihell-railgun-*`; the four
  sibling net-new weapons are equally missing.
- Docs — `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` has no Railgun row; the GDD §4.4
  net-new-weapon note describes the Railgun purely visually.

## Desired change

1. Author `aihell-railgun-fire` and `aihell-railgun-impact` ToneForge recipes,
   bake them, and register both in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` with recorded
   seeds (suggested reserved seeds 32276 and 32277 — the next free values after
   `aihell-arc-impact` at 32275; adjust only if the manifest disagrees).
2. Export `playRailgunFireSound()` and `playRailgunImpactSound()` from
   `src/audio/effects.ts`, add `case 'railgun'` to `playWeaponFireSound`, and add
   `playRailgunImpactSound` to `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`.
3. Add the `impactFx` spec to the `railgun` catalogue entry (sky blue, cue
   `playRailgunImpactSound`), letting `resolveWeaponDefinition` carry it through
   levelling unchanged. No muzzle-flash metadata in this item (see Related work).
4. Update `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, the GDD §4.4/§7.3 weapon notes
   and the README roster, and add/refresh the tests listed under Acceptance
   Criteria.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new `playRailgunFireSound` / `playRailgunImpactSound`
  exports, the `playWeaponFireSound` `railgun` case and the
  `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES` entry.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `impactFx` metadata on the `railgun` catalogue entry
  (colour/radius/duration/cue); companion comment in the net-new-weapons block.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — consume-only; confirm the new metadata survives
  `resolveWeaponDefinition` (existing tests cover the pattern).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-railgun-fire.yaml`,
  `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-railgun-impact.yaml` — new recipes.

Searched `railgun`, `weapon feel`, `muzzle flash` and `SFX`. No open or completed
item supplies a Railgun fire or impact cue: the completed per-weapon "visuals &
feel" items cover the original 11 weapons only, and the Shard Swarm item
explicitly excludes the Railgun. **Partial overlap at most** (shared pipeline
shapes) — no full duplicate, so this item proceeds unchanged.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** the item title and description ask for SFX, so this
  brief delivers the **fire cue and hit cue** only; `impactFx` is included
  because it is the sole carrier for a per-weapon hit cue, and it necessarily
  brings the sky-blue impact flash colour with it. A Railgun muzzle-flash VFX
  spec is **not** in this item (the tracer already has a strong in-flight
  identity) — tracked separately as a low-priority follow-up item
  AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K.
- **Assumption (cue design):** exact frequencies/envelopes are the
  implementer's call within the character descriptions; the seeds are indicative.
- **Risk — pierce spam:** the Railgun can hit up to 5 enemies per shot, each
  calling `resolveWeaponImpactFx`. Mitigation: a short cue plus the shared
  4-voice/150 ms limiter; the acceptance criteria require the chain to read as
  one salvo, and tests pin the dispatch (not a per-frame audio assertion).
- **Risk — baked-asset drift:** forgetting the `build-audio.sh --render` run or
  the seed pinning leaves `build-audio:verify` red. Mitigation: seeds recorded in
  both the manifest and the docs table, plus the committed `checksums.json`.
- **Risk — gain staging:** a heavy launch cue can clip the mix next to frequent
  weapon fire. Mitigation: keep the cue short, gain-stage it against the cannon
  (0.15) and wave-laser (0.18) fire cues, and stay under the 0.5 peak ceiling.
- **Risk — silent regression in gyms:** a scene-level switch could make gym audio
  diverge. Mitigation: the shared dispatcher is the only route; the gym-parity
  and equivalence guards must pass unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** four sibling net-new weapons still lack a feel package
  (`rear_guard`, `broadside`, `heavy_slug` — plus this item's muzzle flash) have
  no dedicated low-priority item or are tracked separately. Recorded as linked
  follow-up opportunities, **not** absorbed here.

## Open decisions for the producer

None blocking. One documented assumption is flagged above (SFX scope; muzzle
flash deferred) — say so if you want the muzzle flash pulled into this item
instead.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context ("no SFX, certainly on
launch, possibly on hit"), the sibling audit item
AH-0MVMJMCQK004BE9T, and a repo audit of the weapon definition, audio
dispatcher, cue manifest and testing seams were sufficient to draft a clear
brief.

- Q: "Which cue does the Railgun currently miss?" — **Answer (repo evidence):**
  both. `playWeaponFireSound` has no `railgun` case
  (`src/audio/effects.ts`, dispatch `default:` no-op) and the catalogue entry has
  no `impactFx` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, railgun block), so fire is silent and
  hits play no cue and only the generic warm-white flash.
  Source: `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`.
- Q: "Does an existing item already cover this?" — **Answer (worklog search):**
  no. The Shard Swarm item AH-0MVMJMCQK004BE9T explicitly excludes the Railgun
  and points at this item; the completed per-weapon feel items cover only the
  original 11 weapons. Source: `wl search railgun`, `wl show
  AH-0MVMJMCQK004BE9T`.
- Q: "Is a muzzle flash required to make the launch audible?" — **Answer
  (research):** no. Audibility comes from the `playWeaponFireSound` dispatcher,
  which needs no definition metadata; `impactFx` is only required to route the
  *hit* cue. Research: inspected `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (muzzle flash is
  gated on `def.muzzleFlash`, VFX only) and `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx`
  (cue lives in `impactFx`). Recorded as the scope assumption above.
- Q: "What cue character fits the Railgun?" — **Answer (design, assumed):** a
  heavy electromagnetic discharge for launch and a short metallic crack with a
  brief ring for impact, distinct from the Wave Laser's beam crack. Evidence: the
  per-weapon cue table in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` shows each weapon
  occupying a deliberately distinct character slot. Producer may redirect.

# Intake brief — Compiled videos cannot be fast forwarded (AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR)

## Headline

Videos produced by `npm run capture` (MediaRecorder WebM/VP9+Opus) are
written **without a Duration element, SeekHead or Cues (seek index)**, so VLC
cannot fast-forward, seek, or even display a usable timeline for them. The fix
is a packet-preserving (`-c copy`) seek-index remux of every successful
capture output before it is delivered.

## Problem statement

Chromium's `MediaRecorder` writes a WebM stream whose Segment Info omits
Duration and whose clusters carry no external Cues/SeekHead index. Most
players tolerate this, but VLC does not: fast-forward/seeking fails,
`ffprobe` reports `duration=N/A`, and the timeline is unusable. Verified on
real capture outputs under `capture-output/` — e.g.
`capture-output/gameplay-2026-10-09T21-32-12-740Z-1.webm` has zero Cues and
zero SeekHead elements (`duration=N/A`), while the ffmpeg-compiled promos
(`capture-output/promo.webm`, `highlight-01.webm`) carry all three and are
seekable (`duration=57.896` etc.).

## Users

- The developer/producer reviewing captured gameplay footage (full runs,
  batch iterations, scenario clips, multi-scene stitched WebMs) in VLC or
  other external players.
- Any consumer of the shipped/archived WebMs who needs to scrub or fast-forward
  them without re-encoding.

User story: *As a developer reviewing captured gameplay, I want to fast-forward
and scrub through the WebM in VLC, so I can jump straight to the segments I
need instead of watching the whole clip.*

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Seekable output**: A WebM produced by `npm run capture` (with an ffmpeg
   available on the host) reports a finite non-zero total duration via
   `ffprobe -show_entries format=duration` (`format.duration`), and its EBML
   structure contains a Cues seek index plus SeekHead referencing Info,
   Tracks and Cues — verified per clip by the capture tool's existing probe.
2. **No quality/content change**: The remux is packet-preserving
   (`-c copy` — no re-encode of VP9 or Opus); codecs, stream layout, and
   decoded frame/timeline content are unchanged (verify codec + duration
   equivalence against a pre-fix capture).
3. **All capture paths benefit**: single clip, `--count` batch iterations,
   `--all-scenarios` scenario clips and the `capture:scenes` multi-scene
   stitched WebM all go through the same sink-finalise seam and are all
   seekable (they share `recording.finalise({ success: true })`).
4. **Graceful degradation**: When no ffmpeg binary can be resolved (this is
   the documented zero-ffmpeg capture environment), the capture still
   succeeds and writes the current unseekable WebM, with a clear warning
   naming the fix and how to enable it — never a hard failure that breaks
   the no-ffmpeg story.
5. **Tests + docs**: Hermetic unit tests for any new pure logic (remux
   invocation argc/verification without real footage), plus an
   integration/e2e verification on a small real clip asserting duration +
   Cues + SeekHead presence; `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (known-limits and
   output sections) and code comments updated; full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Existing documented design decision (docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md
  "No MP4 output (ffmpeg)" and `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` header): "the
  capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg". The recommended approach (a)
  keeps that constraint intact by using only the Playwright-bundled binary;
  Open Question 1 records the producer decision.
- Playwright (an existing devDependency, installed by the documented
  `npm run capture:install`) ships a **bundled ffmpeg binary** that performs
  the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified: the bundled
  `ffmpeg-linux` from the ms-playwright cache produced Duration + Cues +
  SeekHead and `duration=1.895` on a real capture). This is the recommended
  remux tool — no system install needed.
- Long-run clips can be ~1.8 GB; the sink architecture was built to keep node
  memory O(one chunk). A remux pass must stream through ffmpeg (or equivalent)
  and must not buffer the whole clip in node memory.
- Salvaged `.partial.webm` outputs are documented failure paths, not
  deliverables — out of scope.
- UK English in all written output.
- Backfill of already-captured WebMs is out of scope unless the producer
  requests it (recorded as a separate linked item if wanted).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: a pure-JS EBML rewriter or a backfill/`--seekable` CLI is
  larger than the reported bug. Keep the fix to the minimal remux at the
  finalise seam; record extras as linked work items, not scope.
- **Remux failure on huge clips**: a failed remux must not destroy the raw
  capture — write the remuxed file to a temp path and only swap it in on
  success (mirroring the existing `.partial.webm` rename discipline).
- **ffmpeg resolution portability**: resolution order (env → PATH → bundled
  Playwright ffmpeg) must be deterministic and documented; the bundled
  binary path depends on Playwright's install revision, so resolve it
  through the Playwright API rather than hard-coded paths.
- **Validation parity**: structural checks (duration + Cues + SeekHead) are
  automated via ffprobe; a manual VLC fast-forward check on the operator's
  machine is the final behavioural confirmation.
- **Assumption**: the reported VLC behaviour is caused by the missing
  Duration/Cues/SeekHead (confirmed structurally; see Problem statement).
  Compiled promo outputs are unaffected as they are already ffmpeg-produced.

## Existing state

`npm run capture` drives a headless Chromium page: `canvas.captureStream(60)`
→ `MediaRecorder` (VP9/Opus, 8 Mbps), chunks streamed via a bounded sink
(`scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs`) to `<stem>.partial.webm`, renamed into
place by `finalise({ success: true })`. Chromium writes no Duration/Cues.
The promo compiler (`compile-promo.mjs --compile`) already re-encodes/remuxes
its deliverables through a full ffmpeg, so promo/highlight/showreel outputs
are already seekable — only raw capture outputs are affected.

## Desired change

Attach a seek-index remux step at the sink-finalise seam so every successful
capture WebM is made seekable before it is delivered. **Decided approach (a):**
resolve the **Playwright-bundled** ffmpeg first (it is installed by the
documented `npm run capture:install` and is verified to perform this remux),
falling back to `FFMPEG_BIN`/`FFPROBE_BIN` env overrides and then PATH
(mirroring `compile-promo`'s `resolveTools()`), run
`ffmpeg -i <in>.webm -c copy <out>.webm`, swap the result in only on success,
and warn (without failing the capture) when no ffmpeg can be resolved. This
keeps the documented "never invokes a **system** ffmpeg" constraint intact.
Verification reuses the existing probe seam (`capture-probe.mjs`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — `finalise()` seam where a seek-index
  remux would attach (or a sibling module invoked from it)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the two sink finalise call sites
  (single-clip ~L1991 and multi-scene ~L2554); recorder setup ~L2753
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `resolveTools()` ffmpeg-location pattern and
  the `-c copy`-style argv precedent to reuse
- `scripts/capture-probe.mjs` — existing probe seam to extend for
  duration/Cues verification
- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.test.ts` (+ new tests) — hermetic coverage
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update known-limits/output sections

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Spike: automated gameplay video capture
  (headless browser + scripted bot); established the capture pipeline.
- **AH-0MUZQG13S006KL8K** — Capture: video join + highlight selection;
  established output artefacts and the raw-WebM format.
- **AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18** — Pure edit-plan/selection logic in compile-promo;
  supplies the ffmpeg-driving pattern (incl. `resolveTools`).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documents the "no system ffmpeg in the
  capture path" constraint and the output/probe contract.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED — producer decision): **How should the seek-index remux relate
  to the documented "the capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg"
  constraint?** Options:
  - (a) Remux by default using the Playwright-bundled ffmpeg. The bundled
    binary (installed by the documented `npm run capture:install`) already
    performs the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified on a real
    capture: Duration + Cues + SeekHead, `duration=1.895`), so no *system*
    ffmpeg is required and the documented constraint stands literally.
    Degrade gracefully when it cannot be resolved.
  - (b) Remux by default, requiring a full system ffmpeg (compile-promo's
    `resolveTools()` path) and hard-failing the delivery when absent.
  - (c) Pure-JS EBML rewrite (patch Info/Duration, prepend SeekHead,
    append Cues) with no binary dependency at all.

  **Recommended: (a)** — smallest change, verified working, packet-preserving,
  no new dependency, and it preserves the documented constraint. `(b)` breaks
  the zero-ffmpeg capture story; `(c)` is a materially larger new
  WebM-rewriting surface (with 1.8 GB streaming-copy risk) for no benefit the
  bundled binary does not already give.

  **Answer (producer): (a)** — remux by default using the Playwright-bundled
  ffmpeg with graceful degradation. Source: interactive reply to the question
  comment (`intake - question ...` on AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR). The brief,
  ACs and Key Files stand as written; no further changes needed.

- Resolved without asking (answerable from repo convention — recorded as
  intake decisions, not open questions):
  - **Default vs opt-in**: the remux runs by default on every successful
    capture, because the report is about the default `npm run capture`
    output. No `--seekable` flag and no backfill command in scope.
  - **Tool resolution**: env override → bundled Playwright ffmpeg → PATH,
    following compile-promo's existing `resolveTools()` pattern
    (`FFMPEG_BIN` / `FFPROBE_BIN` first).
  - **Out of scope**: salvaged `.partial.webm` failure artefacts; backfilling
    already-captured files.

Pending the producer's answer to Q1 the brief stands as written (all
acceptance criteria are behavioural and hold under any of the three
options); the item is flagged for producer review.

**Q1 answered: (a)** — Playwright-bundled ffmpeg remux by default with
graceful degradation. The brief, ACs and Key Files are final and stand as
written.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUWTNPYJ0031FQE** – capture: include game audio in automated gameplay video (completed)
- **AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ** – ffmpeg compile driver and output validation (completed)
- **AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4** – Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muwmff3c002wobk, absent, acceptance, affected, already (+333 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: 0muwmff3c002wobk, absent, affected, already, answer (+312 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, affected, already, answer, answers (+290 more)

# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `predictIncomingFire`
  on the torus.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances
  and the evade flee direction.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — legacy `evaluateVector`, legacy aim/aim-delta and
  closest-approach paths.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` — re-verify the wrap-jump clamp under the
  torus model; adjust only if double-compensating.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
  `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`,
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — retire/re-purpose `wallMargin`; keep config
  loading tolerant.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + `arena.test.ts` — wrapped enemy bullets, seam-aware
  hostile aim, parity tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — describe the wrap-aware model.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`, plus a
  dedicated wrap-geometry unit test module.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** — "Enemies should be aware of the wrap around" (open
  epic with blocked child slices). Enemy counterpart: wrap-aware enemy movement
  and seam-aware enemy fire. Directly relevant — share the seam maths/helpers
  and sequence work so the bot and enemies land coherently.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed) — the wrap model the game's bullets use.
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO** — "Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour
  tree, predictive dodge/aim" (completed) — the competent layer this change
  extends.
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — "Demo bot: human-like input limits" (completed) —
  the human-like governor whose look-and-feel must be preserved.
- **AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN** — "Predict enemy movement (bot)" (completed) — the
  hazard-velocity tracker whose wrap clamp interacts with the torus model.
- **AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV** — "Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay
  objects as the main game" (open) — bot/gym parity concern; watch for overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: duplicate flapping** — when the raw path and the wrapped path are
  nearly equal, a naive min-distance choice can flip between two seam
  duplicates every tick; mitigated with a small hysteresis/tolerance at near-equal
  lengths (the commitment layer already adds some hysteresis).
- **Risk: `wallMargin` migration ripple** — the knob appears across tunables,
  style-fitting, the tuning UI and saved `bot-tuning.json`; handle removal so
  saved configs keep loading, update the fit mapping, and document the behaviour
  change for old configs.
- **Risk: double-compensation** — `hazardVelocity` clamps wrap jumps today;
  once positions are modelled on the torus, verify the tracker only clamps true
  teleports/respawns and never swallows legitimate seam re-entry.
- **Risk: eval divergence** — the headless arena must mirror the game's wrap
  physics or wrap-aware behaviour earns no eval credit; keep the parity change
  minimal (bullet wrap + seam aim) and covered by `arena.test.ts`.
- **Scope-creep guard** — out of scope: game physics changes, non-torus
  pathfinding/routing, scripted wrap manœuvres, and any enemy/wrap changes
  beyond the arena-parity bump. Anything extra found becomes a linked work item,
  not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: dimensions** — the bot already receives playfield dimensions via
  tunables (`playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`, 960×540), so the torus needs no
  snapshot changes.
- **Assumption: seam maths reuse** — the enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8)
  will have developed wrapped-delta helpers; reuse/adapt rather than duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of wrap-awareness for the bot? (a) Movement/steering only. (b) +
  seam-aware aim/targeting. (c) Full torus model — plus seam-aware threat/hazard
  prediction." — Answer (Map): "(c) Full torus model". Source: producer reply on
  the work item (comment thread AH-C0MVR682R00022NOC). Research: steering walls
  in `botDecision.ts` + `steering.ts`, raw Euclidean geometry throughout
  (`goals.ts`, `worldModel.ts`, `behaviours.ts`), enemy wrap epic
  AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 in flight.
- Q2: "Should the bot deliberately *use* the seam as a manœuvre, or merely stop
  avoiding edges?" — Answer (Map): "Use it when net-positive". Source: producer
  reply on the work item. Research: nearest-wrapped-path selection yields
  net-positive seam use naturally; no scripted trick, human-like governor
  unchanged.
- Q3: "Should the headless eval arena be brought to wrap-parity with the game so
  eval measures wrap-aware play?" — Answer (Map): "Yes". Source: producer reply
  on the work item. Research: `arena.ts` culls enemy bullets off-field and aims
  hostile fire at the raw player position — both diverge from the game.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** – Enemies should be aware of the wrap around (open)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** – Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
